newsitem.title: GERMANY: Veba confident of higher profits in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Veba confident of higher profits in 1997.

text.p: German utility and telecommunications group Veba AG said on Tuesday it expected to be able to raise its profits for 1997 as it continues to take measures to cut costs and improve efficiency.

"Because of the overall positive development of the first quarter and despite the difficult start in the chemical sector we are confident of being able to raise earnings again for the full year of 1997," the company said.
"Continued measures to cut costs and raise efficiency as well as further optimisation of (our) portfolio will also contribute to the earnings improvement," Veba said.
Veba said its first quarter net profit after minorities rose seven percent to 486 million marks while pre-tax profit rose 6.8 percent to 1.08 billion marks.
Higher profits from the oil and trading, transport, and service segments more than compensated for a "significant earnings decrease" in chemicals, which came amid rising raw materials costs.
The company also said its telecommunications interests, still in their build-up phase, ended the period at a loss "according to plan."

Sales in the first quarter rose 7.8 percent to 19.624 billion marks, with oil sales showing the biggest advance to rise 19.1 percent to 4.925 billion marks. In the chemicals sector, sales dropped by 1.6 percent to 2.6 billion marks.
